newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Overnight guilders nosedive on credit quota expiry.
newsitem.headline: Overnight guilders nosedive on credit quota expiry.

text.p: Overnight guilder rates nosedived on Thursday as market players cashed in savings on the eve of the three-month credit quota expiry, but were seen regaining their customary levels on Friday.
Dutch call money was quoted at 2.0 percent bid, 75 basis points down on Wednesday's rate and well below the current special advances rate of 2.50 percent.

Dealers said trades were being done at between 2.0 and 2.125 percent. "It's not unusual for call to come down sharply on the last day of a credit quota pact, although this time the fluctuation is quite extreme," one said.

Call money rates were stuck at highs for most of the week, with traders speculating some major banks had used up their quota of borrowings from the Dutch central bank, forcing them to seek recourse to overnight funds.
"Overall the central bank will have pegged the quota at an appropriate level, but some banks apparently feared they were not going to make it," a dealer said.
He said overnight guilder rates, which started falling late Wednesday, had maintained a steady slide.
But they were seen recovering to around 2.68 percent bid on Friday on the back of the new secured loans quota.
"It's all change tomorrow with a new secured loans quota, new cash reserve and new special advances pact," a dealer said.
The new cash reserve, pegged at 5.06 billion guilders, runs until October 31.
This pact effectively functions in the opposite way to the credit quota, creaming off surplus money market funds to keep rates steady and support the guilder.
The rate on the latest special advances pact, a short running facility used to finetune market liquidity, will be set at 1400 GMT today. Dealers expect an unchanged 2.50 percent.
The guilder firmed a touch against the mark, trading at 112.21 per 100 marks from Wednesday's 112.22 fixing.
